 Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise cleared of structural damage; Aleksandar Pavlović rested as precaution
 FC Bayern escaped some bad news (so far).
 by CSmith1919 Nov 3, 2026, 8:03 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images Part Of Atlético Madrid vs. Bayern Munich: 2026/27 Champions League full coverage see all updates CSmith1919 Chuck Smith is the site manager for Bavarian Football Works, where he began writing in 2017. He is the author of The Daily Schmankerl, the longest-running daily Bayern Munich column in English, and also writes The Weekend Warm-Up. In addition to covering Bayern Munich news and providing commentary on Bayern Munich, the Bundesliga, and the German national team. He brings more than 30 years of sports-writing experience to the site. Over the course of his career, he has written for numerous newspapers and websites. Bayern Munich have received some encouraging injury news, with Aaron Danks providing updates on Aleksandar Pavlović and Michael Olise.
 According to Danks (via @iMiaSanMia ), Pavlović is dealing with a small issue, prompting the coachingand medical staff to take a cautious approach rather than risk aggravating it. With an important stretch of fixtures ahead, there is little reason to push the midfielder unnecessarily, particularly if giving him additional recovery time can prevent a more significant problem.
 The news surrounding Olise is even more encouraging, as he is in the starting XI versus Atlético Madrid. Danks confirmed that the Frenchman has no structural injury and is ready to play. His recent discomfort was simply a matter of pain management rather than an underlying physical issue.
 That should come as a significant relief for Bayern Munich, considering Olise’s importance to the attack. Losing him for an extended period would have been a major blow and another significant hit for an already depleted roster to take.
